newsitem.title: USA: IMF declines to comment on German deficit report.
newsitem.headline: IMF declines to comment on German deficit report.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday declined to comment on a German newspaper report that the IMF believed Germany would meet budget deficit targets needed to sign up for Europe's single currency.
"We cannot comment on this," a spokesman said. "We do not comment on newspaper reports."

The Berliner Zeitung, quoting IMF experts, said in a report released ahead of publication on Wednesday that the IMF believed that the 1997 budget deficit would initially come in at 3.1 percent of gross domestic product.
But "statistical refinements" would revise the figure down to three percent, the deficit target laid down in the Maastricht treaty on a single European currency.

German officials have insisted that they will meet the Maastricht target. But the IMF said in April it expected a budget deficit of 3.3 percent of gross domestic product, down from 3.8 percent in 1996.
